solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Film fan regularly entertains friend, an African resident

indicators.note: entertains means the regular letters hold another piece inside, as a host holds a guest
regularly means taking every other letter of the words film fan

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A movie buff is hosting a friend, apparently someone from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks I, M, A from 'Film fan'; 'entertains' puts PAL inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: This antelope lives wild in Africa, so it is an African resident in the animal sense.

clue.text: European journalists sustained by very good beverage

indicators.note: sustained by means held up from either side, so the journalists sit inside the other piece

parts.note: SO means very, as in 'so kind'; the setter stretches it to stand for very good
the press is journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Reporters kept going on a fine drink, like a newsroom running on coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sustained by' reads as 'fuelled by' but means held between the two letters of the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong black coffee is a hot drink, a type of beverage.

clue.text: Right snappy creature discussed gardening device

indicators.note: discussed means the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: right is proper, and a snappy creature is a gator (alligator); said together, proper gator

explanation.surface: A proper snapping reptile is being talked over, though it turns out to be garden kit.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a heated or covered tray in which gardeners raise seedlings, a piece of garden equipment.

clue.text: Article kept in writer's stacks

indicators.note: kept in means one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: the writer's is the setter's, so 'my'
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article is filed among an author's piles of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's' means the setter's own, so MY, with AN 'kept in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally 'stacks of' means a great number of, a synonym for lots.

clue.text: Old comedian has to flog award after ending in arrears

indicators.note: after means the flogging and award pieces come after that final letter
ending in means take only the final letter of arrears

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to flog them
a laurel is an honour or award, from the victor's wreath

explanation.surface: A debt-ridden old comic has to sell off his prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flog' looks like British slang for sell; here it means beat, TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin half of Laurel and Hardy was a film comic of the 1920s and 30s.

clue.text: Excited with silver, admitting gold lost in second half

indicators.note: admitting means letting the other piece inside

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: lost in second half means the word gold drops its last two letters

parts.note: taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: An athlete is thrilled with silver, conceding the gold slipped away after half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold' is taken as a word here, not the symbol AU or OR; 'lost in second half' drops its back half.
explanation.definitionFit: Being eager and full of anticipation is a synonym for being excited.

clue.text: Sort of book one's beginning after a couple of beers?

indicators.note: after means the beer piece comes before the opening letter

parts.note: a quart is two pints, so a couple of pints of beer

indicators.note: beginning means just the first letter of one

explanation.surface: Someone starts reading only after a couple of pints.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a book format, with each printed sheet folded twice to give four leaves.

clue.text: Father's seen fliers, with a section on fish oil

parts.note: pa is father
the RAF, Royal Air Force, are fliers
a fin is a part on a fish

explanation.surface: Dad has seen birds, and a part of a fish oil too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fliers' are the RAF, Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fuel oil refined from petroleum, known in the US as kerosene.

clue.text: Wrongdoer's pile covers acres, after crooked activity

indicators.note: covers means the money piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a mint, like a pile, is a large sum of money

indicators.note: after crooked activity means the letters of acres have been bent out of shape

explanation.surface: A villain's fortune spans many acres, earned from shady dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pile' means a fortune here, not a heap; 'after crooked activity' is a long-winded anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain or scoundrel is someone who does wrong; the 's stands for 'is'.

clue.text: Perhaps a boxer, when retired, eats top-class cheese

indicators.note: eats means the other piece is taken inside
when retired means going back, so the piece is read backwards

parts.note: a boxer is perhaps a dog, so a dog
U is upper-class, top drawer

explanation.surface: A fighter tucks into fancy cheese after hanging up his gloves.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer is the dog breed, not a fighter. 'when retired' turns A DOG into GODA; 'eats' takes in U.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a mild yellow Dutch cheese, named after a town in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Decline a piece of silverware?

parts.note: a cup or trophy is sporting silverware

explanation.surface: Asks whether a sports cup counts as a piece of silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasting away or withering is a form of decline.

clue.text: Country song as popular on the flip-side?

indicators.note: on the flip-side means the whole thing turned over, read from the end

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
as, in the sense 'for example', is e.g.
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A country-music song released as the B-side of a single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the flip-side' reads AIR EG IN backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This West African state is a nation, a synonym for country.

clue.text: Turkey transporter

definitions.meaning: a turkey is a flop or fool
a donkey carries loads, a beast of burden

explanation.surface: A vehicle for carrying turkeys.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fool, like a turkey, and a donkey used for carrying goods.

clue.text: Relative, heading away from Daryl and Charlie, gets bakery item

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother, a relative

indicators.note: heading away from means Daryl loses its first letter

parts.note: a charlie is a fool in British slang

explanation.surface: A family member leaves Daryl and Charlie behind and gets bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' is British slang for a fool, OAF.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a brown bread made with malted grains, a type of loaf sold at a baker's.

clue.text: Football team playing on Sat, home perhaps

indicators.note: playing means the letters of on Sat are being moved around

parts.note: a villa is a type of home

explanation.surface: A football club playing at home on Saturday.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is a Birmingham club in English football.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a professional English football club based in Birmingham.

clue.text: Fearful blow which martial artist might bear

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, fearful
a belt is a hard blow

explanation.surface: A frightening strike of the kind a martial artist might have to endure.
explanation.definitionFit: In judo and karate a coloured sash marks grade, and a beginner wears this one.

clue.text: United high-flyer nets nothing as sub

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in team names

indicators.note: nets means catches inside, as in a net

parts.note: a bat flies by night
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A star United player scores nothing and is put on as substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sub' looks like a football substitute; it is a submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a German submarine of the world wars, so 'sub' is short for submarine.

clue.text: New dune formed flanking English river

indicators.note: flanking means sitting on both sides of the other piece
formed means the letters of dune are shaped anew

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, England

explanation.surface: A fresh sand dune built up beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like an anagram signal but is the definition; 'formed' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not yet tried out is new, a near synonym.

clue.text: Rising rubbish needs tip

indicators.note: to tip something is to overturn it, so the word is flipped end to end

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: A growing heap of rubbish needs a dump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like a British rubbish dump, and 'Rising' like the reversal signal; in fact 'tip' turns ROT over and 'Rising' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocky hill on moorland is a piece of high ground, a rise in the land.

clue.text: Child, having eaten when empty, becomes full

parts.note: a lad is a boy, a child

indicators.note: when empty means only the outside letters of eaten remain

explanation.surface: A child who has eaten on an empty stomach ends up full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when empty' keeps only E and N of 'eaten'.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavily loaded or weighed down is the sense of full here.

clue.text: When annually off, chaplain's learned equestrian event

indicators.note: off means those letters are taken away

parts.note: a padre is an army chaplain
p.a., per annum, means annually
sage means wise, learned

explanation.surface: A chaplain's wisdom when the yearly allowance is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes PA from PADRES SAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the horse-riding discipline of trained movements, an Olympic event.

clue.text: Worker progressed poorly, given old Spanish wine

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker
ran means went along, progressed
ill means poorly, unwell

explanation.surface: A struggling worker is handed a glass of old Spanish wine.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a black grape and the red wine made from it, notably in Rioja.

clue.text: Cat's cry circulates commotion in grassland area

indicators.note: circulates means goes round the other piece

parts.note: a mew is the thin cry a cat makes
ado is fuss, commotion

explanation.surface: A cat's yowl spreads alarm across a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of grass for hay or grazing is an area of grassland.

clue.text: "Long time no see" (finally returning)

indicators.note: returning means read backwards
finally means the last letter of see

explanation.surface: The greeting 'long time no see', with a bracketed stage direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E from 'see'; 'returning' reads NO E backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An age or era of immense length is a very long period.

clue.text: There's appreciation in college about what composer does?

indicators.note: in means the thanks go inside
about means turning back, read backwards

parts.note: Eton is the famous English school, Eton College
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: Asks whether thanks given in a college marks what a composer does.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thank you, and Eton is the famous English school.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing music down in score form is a composer's job, so the definition is a cryptic description.

clue.text: Dog's keen to remove confines of rein

parts.note: sharp means keen, as a blade

indicators.note: to remove confines of means drop the outer letters of rein

explanation.surface: A dog eager to slip its lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to remove confines of' leaves EI from 'rein'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a wrinkly Chinese dog breed; the 's stands for 'is'.

clue.text: Swimmer with soft skin

parts.note: p, piano, means soft in music
an eel is a swimming fish

explanation.surface: A swimmer with smooth skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The rind of a fruit is its skin.

clue.text: Tend to kid and tease outside near son

indicators.note: outside means the teasing piece goes round the rest

parts.note: to bait is to tease
by means near

explanation.surface: Someone tends to joke around, teasing a nearby son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tend to kid' looks like 'is inclined to joke'; it means look after a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking after a youngster while parents are out is child-minding.

clue.text: Junk-mail Mike put in short beige container

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the other piece
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: buff is a pale yellowish-beige colour
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Mike stuffs junk mail into a small beige box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts BUFF to BUF; M is 'put in'.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for useless paperwork or leaflets, much like unwanted post.

clue.text: Felon's inside, primarily planning early escape with mate

indicators.note: inside means the middle letters of felon, its outer letters gone
primarily means the first letters of planning and early

explanation.surface: A prisoner, inside, first plots an early breakout with a cellmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mate' looks like a fellow inmate; it is a romantic partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away secretly to marry is to flee with a partner.

clue.text: Ray perhaps hit hard by difficult situation

parts.note: to lam is to thrash, hit hard
a plight is a predicament

explanation.surface: Ray, perhaps a man, is struck by hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name; it is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray of the glow from a lamp is an example of this light.
